title: The invariant-open quotient of an etale atlas
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $X$ be an algebraic space over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], and let $p:h_U\to X$ be a representable surjective etale scheme atlas. Give $|X|$ its field-valued point classes and atlas topology [def-a1-space-point-topology]. For any open subset $O\subseteq|X|$, let $V\subseteq U$ be the open subscheme with underlying set $|p|^{-1}(O)$ [def-weil-open-immersion]. Let $R=U\times_XU$ with projections $s,t:R\to U$, and let $R_V=V\times_{U,s}R\times_{t,U}V$ [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Then $s^{-1}(V)=t^{-1}(V)=R_V$ as open subschemes of $R$, the restricted projections $R_V\rightrightarrows V$ form an etale equivalence relation, and its fppf sheaf quotient $J=V/R_V$ [def-weil-pbc-sheafification, def-pc-fppf-site] is an algebraic space. The map $h_V\to J$ is representable surjective etale, the induced map $j:J\to X$ is representable by open immersions, and its point image is $O$. Identifying $J$ with the image subfunctor of $j$ gives an open subspace of $X$ [def-a1-space-open-subspace].

proof.text: The representing kernel-pair square makes the coequalizer descent f into X sectionwise injective: lift two quotient sections to atlas sections, use hR to join equal images by a relation section, and apply the coequalizer equation. Sheafify its range as a subpresheaf of the already existing fppf sheaf X, using Mathlib Subfunctor.sheafify and its universal property. This constructs Q and its quotient unit in Type u without a global sheafification instance. Apply etale_atlas_presentation to obtain the original relation, surjective etale projections, and the comparison isomorphism Q to X with atlas compatibility.

proof.text: The final topology makes the inverse image W of O along p open. Set V to the actual scheme restriction to W and i to its inclusion. A field-valued scheme section has the same point class as the residue-field map of its image, by the factorization from Spec of a field. This proves naturality of schemePointMap and makes the inverse-image opens under s and t equal, using hR.w. For the canonical double restricted relation, invariance factors the second endpoint of the first pullback through i; the first projection from the double pullback is therefore an isomorphism. Transport the first pullback square across this isomorphism. Its open range and invariance give the second pullback square by the open-immersion pullback criterion, with the very same relation-to-R map.

source.place: Tag 03BZ (lemma-open-subspaces), inverse construction; field-point calculation uses Tags 03BU/03BV/03H5 and schemes.tex field-valued point factorization.

proof.text: Open immersions are etale. Apply etale_pullback_relation_presheaf to i: it gives the canonical restricted projections, monicity, their equivalence-relation property, etaleness, and the sectionwise injective map v of quotient presheaves. The composite v followed by f embeds the restricted quotient presheaf in X. Sheafify this subpresheaf inside X exactly as in step 1 to construct J and its unit eta, with the required hom-set bijections.

source.place: Tag 03BZ (lemma-open-subspaces), inverse construction; field-point calculation uses Tags 03BU/03BV/03H5 and schemes.tex field-valued point factorization.

proof.text: Apply etale_relation_restriction_quotient to Q and J to obtain the monomorphism beta. Etaleness supplies flatness and local finite presentation, so etale_relation_finding_opens also gives a map alpha from J to Q representable by open immersions. The two maps have the same composite with the quotient atlas. Cancel the presheaf coequalizer projection, then use injectivity of the hom-set bijection for eta to show alpha equals beta. Thus alpha is both monic and representable by open immersions.

source.place: Tag 03BZ (lemma-open-subspaces), inverse construction; field-point calculation uses Tags 03BU/03BV/03H5 and schemes.tex field-valued point factorization.

proof.text: Apply etale_relation_quotient to the restricted relation and the constructed unit eta. This proves J is an algebraic space and its canonical atlas q is representable surjective etale. Compose alpha with the original presentation isomorphism to obtain j. The two atlas-compatibility equations prove q followed by j equals i followed by p. Transport representing squares along that isomorphism to prove j is representable by open immersions; it is also monic.

source.place: Tag 03BZ (lemma-open-subspaces), inverse construction; field-point calculation uses Tags 03BU/03BV/03H5 and schemes.tex field-valued point factorization.

proof.text: Prove directly that any representably surjective scheme-source map is surjective on point classes: test against a field-valued representative, lift the closed point to the representing surjective scheme, and use the residue-field comparison and the pullback equation. Applied to q and p, this computes pointImage j as the range of schemePointMap of q followed by j, hence as p applied to the range of i, namely p applied to the inverse image of O, which is O. The already defined mapPoint is used only to transport equality of quotient-point classes. Monicity makes Subfunctor.toRange j an isomorphism. Transport each representing square along that isomorphism to see the range inclusion is representable by open immersions; package the range as an OpenSubspace.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q18-06d905156 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read Stacks 03BZ(1) and 02WU. The six steps follow 03BZ(1) exactly. Step 1, atlas-presentation (0262): kernel pair, surjective étale s and t, U/R≅X; openness of |p|^-1(O) comes from the final topology. Step 2, 01JR: the preimages under s and t are equal open subschemes, and R_V is their intersection; elementary. Step 3, 02GP plus restriction-quotient: g étale, so R_V is an étale equivalence relation and J→U/R is injective; the surjectivity clause is not used. Step 4, 02WW: the hypotheses, a monic equivalence relation with étale s and t, hold; J is algebraic and q is surjective étale. Step 5, 02WU: étale gives flat+lfp, and s and t are surjective by 0262; the open-immersion conclusion is transported along U/R≅X. Step 6: |q| and |p| are surjective by the 03H5 clause of point-open-calculus; im|j| = |p|(|p|^-1 O) = O; the image subfunctor satisfies the open-subspace definition. Only the surjectivity clause of point-open-calculus is used, and no proof_dep closure contains the item. Edge cases checked: O empty, O=|X|, p=id, disconnected atlas. Tags and labels are verified. The statement, stmt_deps and blueprint are unchanged from live, where the item is still unsplit; there is no repair note and no new nodes. lem-trf-etale-open-chart-morphism-descent is related but does not state the quotient J, the atlas or the point image, so it is not a duplicate. Batch-5 check: the restriction-quotient, quotient and finding-opens trf nodes, and def-trf-algebraic-space reached via atlas-presentation, are generic algebraic-space foundations (02WT/045Z/02WW/02WU). Neither assumption leaf gives them, and their closures hold only fppf descent and relation-quotient lemmas, no cohomological trace-formula or duality content. Accepted, with the three declared tool_uses. No SGA.

lean.statement: theorem space_invariant_open_quotient {S : Scheme.{u}} (X : AlgebraicSpace S) (U : Over S) (p : yoneda.obj U ⟶ X.obj.obj) (hp : IsEtale p) (hsur : IsSurjective p) (O : Set (Point X.obj.obj)) (hO : IsOpen O) (R : Over S) (s t : R ⟶ U) (hR : IsPullback (yoneda.map s) (yoneda.map t) p p) : ∃ (V : Over S) (i : V ⟶ U), IsOpenImmersion i.left ∧ Set.range i.left.base = schemePointMap p ⁻¹' O ∧ ∃ (RV : Over S) (r : RV ⟶ R) (sV tV : RV ⟶ V), IsPullback r sV s i ∧ IsPullback r tV t i ∧ Mono (prod.lift sV tV) ∧ (∀ T : Over S, Equivalence (fun a b : T ⟶ V ↦ ∃ v : T ⟶ RV, v ≫ sV = a ∧ v ≫ tV = b)) ∧ Etale sV.left ∧ Etale tV.left ∧ ∃ (J : Sheaf (Scheme.fppfTopology.over S) (Type u)) (η : coequalizer (yoneda.map sV) (yoneda.map tV) ⟶ J.obj), (∀ G : Sheaf (Scheme.fppfTopology.over S) (Type u), Function.Bijective (fun a : J.obj ⟶ G.obj ↦ η ≫ a)) ∧ IsAlgebraicSpace J ∧ IsEtale (coequalizer.π (yoneda.map sV) (yoneda.map tV) ≫ η) ∧ IsSurjective (coequalizer.π (yoneda.map sV) (yoneda.map tV) ≫ η) ∧ ∃ j : J.obj ⟶ X.obj.obj, (coequalizer.π (yoneda.map sV) (yoneda.map tV) ≫ η) ≫ j = yoneda.map i ≫ p ∧ IsRepresentableWith (fun _ _ f ↦ IsOpenImmersion f.left) j ∧ pointImage j = O ∧ IsIso (Subfunctor.toRange j) ∧ ∃ A : OpenSubspace X, A.val = Subfunctor.range j
lean.note: The supplied hR specifies an arbitrary scheme representative of U ×_X U. The conclusion constructs the invariant open subscheme and a common representative RV of both open pullbacks, with both cartesian squares; these also identify RV with the double restricted relation. It constructs the quotient and its sheafification unit, rather than assuming existence of global sheafification. The final clauses identify the quotient with the image subfunctor as an OpenSubspace.
